{"type": "text", "text": "Base directory for this skill: /logs/agent/sessions/skills/powerpoint-pptx

## When to Use

Use when the main artifact is a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation or `.pptx` deck, especially when layouts, templates, placeholders, notes, comments, charts, extraction, editing, or final visual quality matter.

## Core Rules

### 1. Choose the workflow before touching the deck

- Reading text, editing an existing deck, rebuilding from a template, and creating from scratch are different jobs with different failure modes.
- For text extraction or inspection, read the deck before editing it.
- Text extraction plus thumbnail-style visual inspection is safer than editing from shape assumptions alone.
- For template-driven work, inventory the deck before replacing content.
- For deep edits, remember a `.pptx` file is OOXML with separate parts for slides, layouts, masters, media, notes, and comments.
- If a template exists, template fidelity beats generic slide-design instincts.
- Reusing or duplicating a good existing slide is often safer than rebuilding it and hoping the theme still matches.

### 2. Inventory the deck before replacing content

- Count the reusable layouts, real placeholders, notes, comments, media, and recurring typography or color patterns first.
- Placeholder indexes and layout indexes are not portable assumptions.
- Inspect the actual slide or template before targeting title, body, chart, or image shapes.
- Speaker notes, comments, and linked assets can live outside the visible slide surface.
- A missing or wrong placeholder target can silently land content in the wrong box or wrong layer.
- Master and layout settings can override local slide edits, so the visible problem is not always on the slide you are editing.

### 3. Match content to the actual placeholders

- Count the actual content pieces before choosing a layout.
- Pick layouts based on the real number of ideas, columns, images, or charts the slide needs.
- Do not force two ideas into a three-column slide or cram dense text under a chart.
- Category counts and data series lengths must match or charts will break in ugly ways.
- Explicit sizing beats wishful thinking: text boxes, images, and charts need real space, not "it should fit".
- Do not choose a layout with more placeholders than the content can meaningfully fill.
- Quote layouts are for real quotes, and image-led layouts are for slides that actually have images.
- For chart-, table-, or image-heavy slides, full-slide or two-column layouts are usually safer than stacking dense text above the visual.

### 4. Preserve the deck's visual language

- Theme, master, and layout files usually decide fonts, colors, and hierarchy more than any one slide does.
- Start from the deck's actual theme, fonts, spacing, and aspect ratio instead of improvising a new style.
- Reuse the deck's own alignment and spacing system instead of inventing a second visual language.
- Use common fonts for portability and strong contrast for readability.
- Preserve the template's visual logic first; originality matters less than not breaking the deck's existing language.
- Combining slides from multiple sources requires normalizing themes, masters, and alignment afterward.

### 5. Run content QA and visual QA separately

- Text overflow, bad alignment, clipped shapes, weak contrast, and placeholder leftovers are normal first-pass failures.
- Run both content QA and visual QA; missing text and broken layout are different failure classes.
- Render or inspect the actual deck output before delivery when layout matters.
- Search for leftover template junk, sample labels, and placeholder text before calling the deck finished.
- Check notes, comments, labels, legends, and chart/table semantics separately from the visual pass.
- A deck can pass text extraction and still fail on overlap, clipping, wrong theme inheritance, or broken notes.
- Thumbnail grids and rendered slides usually reveal layout bugs faster than code or text inspection.
- Assume the first render is wrong and do at least one fix-and-verify cycle before calling the deck finished.
- Re-check affected slides after each fix because one spacing change often creates another issue.

### 6. Keep decks portable and review-safe

- Template masters can override direct edits in surprising ways.
- Complex effects may degrade across PowerPoint, LibreOffice, and conversion pipelines, so keep important content robust without them.
- Image sizing, font substitution, and placeholder mismatch are common reasons a deck looks good in code and bad on screen.
- Notes, comments, linked media, and merged decks can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.

## Common Traps

- Placeholder text and sample charts often survive template reuse if not explicitly replaced.
- Directly editing one slide can fail if the real issue lives in the master or layout.
- Charts, icons, and text boxes need enough space; near-collisions are usually visible only after rendering.
- Layout indexes vary by template, so built-in assumptions from one deck often break in another.
- A missing placeholder or wrong shape target can silently put content in the wrong place.
- Counting the text ideas after choosing the layout usually leads to empty placeholders, weak hierarchy, or leftover template junk.
- Font substitution can move line breaks and wreck careful spacing.
- Speaker notes, comments, and linked media can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
- A deck can pass text inspection and still fail visually because of overlap, contrast, or edge clipping.
- Editing from one slide alone can miss the real source of truth in the theme, master, or layout definitions.
- Choosing a quote, comparison, or multi-column layout without matching content usually makes the deck look templated rather than intentional.
- Combining or duplicating slides without checking masters and themes can create subtle inconsistency slide by slide.
- Aspect-ratio mismatches like `16:9` versus `4:3` can shift every placement decision even when each slide looks locally reasonable.

- `design` — Visual direction and layout decisions.
- `brief` — Concise business messaging for slide narratives.

Generative AI's emergence is not a sudden event but the culmination of decades of technological progress:

- **Six decades of Moore's Law** delivered the compute horsepower to process exaflops of data.
- **Four decades of the internet** (accelerated by COVID) produced trillions of tokens of training data.

The $100M pre-product seed round returned. Cracks appeared: artists challenged machine-generated IP, Washington debated regulation, and a whisper spread that generative AI was not actually useful — products fell short of expectations with terrible user retention.

## Early Commercial Traction Despite Skepticism

Despite the discontent, generative AI has had a more successful commercial start than SaaS, with **>$1 billion in revenue from startups alone** — a milestone that took SaaS years, not months, to reach. Standout successes include:

- **ChatGPT**: Fastest-growing application in history, with strong product-market fit among students and developers.
- **Midjourney**: Reported hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue with a team of just 11 people.
- **Character.ai**: Popularized AI entertainment and companionship; users spend an average of **2 hours per session** in-app.

However, these successes don't change the reality that many AI companies lack product-market fit or sustainable competitive advantage.

Mobile app retention data reveals a stark gap between established consumer apps and AI-first companies:

| Candy Crush | Incumbent | 32% |
| Duolingo | Incumbent | 30% |
| **Incumbent Median** | — | **51%** |
| Character.ai | AI-First | 41% |
| Runway | AI-First | 27% |
| Remini | AI-First | 14% |
| ChatGPT | AI-First | 14% |
| Lensa | AI-First | 12% |
| **AI-First Median** | — | **14%** |

- **The market is shifting from Act 1 (technology-out) to Act 2 (customer-back)**, where foundation models become components of comprehensive, workflow-integrated solutions rather than standalone products.

AI researchers became rockstars, hacker houses overflowed with autonomous agents and companionship chatbots, and the arXiv printing press became so prolific that researchers jokingly called for a pause on publications.
17	
18	But excitement quickly turned to hysteria. Every company became an "AI copilot." Inboxes filled with undifferentiated pitches for "AI Salesforce" and "AI Adobe." The $100M pre-product seed round returned. 19

21	
22	Despite the discontent, generative AI has had a more successful commercial start than SaaS, with **>$1 billion in revenue from startups alone** — a milestone that took SaaS years, not months, to reach. Standout successes include:

78	**Act 1 (Technology-Out):** The discovery of foundation models as a new "hammer" led to a wave of novelty apps — lightweight demonstrations of cool technology. These apps used foundation models as the entire solution and often lacked stickiness.

"""Build the Sequoia GenAI Act Two presentation."""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.chart.data import ChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
import copy

# ── Palette ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BLACK       = RGBColor(0x0D, 0x0D, 0x0D)
WHITE       = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
SEQ_RED     = RGBColor(0xE8, 0x1C, 0x2E)   # Sequoia brand red
DARK_GRAY   = RGBColor(0x2B, 0x2B, 0x2B)
MID_GRAY    = RGBColor(0x55, 0x55, 0x55)
LIGHT_GRAY  = RGBColor(0xF4, 0xF4, 0xF4)
ACCENT_BLUE = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x56, 0xDB)
INCUMB_COLOR = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x56, 0xDB)  # blue for incumbents
AI_COLOR     = RGBColor(0xE8, 0x1C, 0x2E)  # red for AI-first
ACT1_BG      = RGBColor(0xF0, 0xF4, 0xFF)
ACT2_BG      = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xF0, 0xF1)

SLIDE_W = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_H = Inches(7.5)

# ── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def new_prs():
    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width  = SLIDE_W
    prs.slide_height = SLIDE_H
    return prs


def blank_layout(prs):
    return prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank


def add_rect(slide, l, t, w, h, fill=None, line=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(1, l, t, w, h)  # MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.RECTANGLE
    shape.line.fill.background()
    if fill:
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill
    else:
        shape.fill.background()
    if line:
        shape.line.color.rgb = line
        shape.line.width = Pt(0.75)
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


def add_text_box(slide, text, l, t, w, h,
                 font_name="Calibri", size=18, bold=False,
                 color=BLACK, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                 wrap=True, italic=False):
    txb = slide.shapes.add_textbox(l, t, w, h)
    txb.word_wrap = wrap
    tf = txb.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.name = font_name
    run.font.size = Pt(size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    return txb


def add_slide_number(slide, num, total=8):
    add_text_box(slide, f"{num} / {total}",
                 SLIDE_W - Inches(1.2), SLIDE_H - Inches(0.4),
                 Inches(1.0), Inches(0.3),
                 size=9, color=MID_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)


def add_footer_bar(slide, label="Sequoia Capital  |  September 2023"):
    """Thin bottom bar with attribution."""
    bar = add_rect(slide, 0, SLIDE_H - Inches(0.38), SLIDE_W, Inches(0.38), fill=DARK_GRAY)
    add_text_box(slide, label,
                 Inches(0.35), SLIDE_H - Inches(0.35),
                 Inches(8), Inches(0.32),
                 size=9, color=WHITE)


def header_bar(slide, height=Inches(0.08)):
    add_rect(slide, 0, 0, SLIDE_W, height, fill=SEQ_RED)


def section_tag(slide, text, l, t):
    add_text_box(slide, text.upper(),
                 l, t, Inches(4), Inches(0.3),
                 size=8, bold=True, color=SEQ_RED)


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 1 – Title
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
def slide_title(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout(prs))

    # Full-bleed dark background
    add_rect(slide, 0, 0, SLIDE_W, SLIDE_H, fill=DARK_GRAY)

    # Red left accent bar
    add_rect(slide, 0, 0, Inches(0.18), SLIDE_H, fill=SEQ_RED)

    # Title
    add_text_box(slide,
                 "Generative AI's Act Two",
                 Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(12), Inches(1.4),
                 font_name="Calibri", size=52, bold=True, color=WHITE)

    # Subtitle
    add_text_box(slide,
                 "From Technology Hammer to Real Value",
                 Inches(0.5), Inches(2.95), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
                 font_name="Calibri", size=28, bold=False, color=RGBColor(0xCC, 0xCC, 0xCC))

    # Red divider
    add_rect(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(3.85), Inches(5), Inches(0.05), fill=SEQ_RED)

    # Attribution block
    add_text_box(slide, "Sonya Huang  ·  Pat Grady  ·  GPT-4",
                 Inches(0.5), Inches(4.05), Inches(9), Inches(0.4),
                 size=14, color=RGBColor(0xAA, 0xAA, 0xAA))
    add_text_box(slide, "Sequoia Capital  ·  September 2023",
                 Inches(0.5), Inches(4.5), Inches(9), Inches(0.4),
                 size=14, color=RGBColor(0xAA, 0xAA, 0xAA))

    # Tag line
    add_text_box(slide,
                 "Confidential — For Discussion Purposes Only",
                 Inches(0.5), SLIDE_H - Inches(0.7), Inches(9), Inches(0.35),
                 size=10, color=RGBColor(0x77, 0x77, 0x77), italic=True)

    return slide


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 2 – Decades of Convergence
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
def slide_convergence(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout(prs))
    add_rect(slide, 0, 0, SLIDE_W, SLIDE_H, fill=WHITE)
    header_bar(slide)

    section_tag(slide, "Foundation", Inches(0.5), Inches(0.18))

    add_text_box(slide,
                 "Six Decades of Technological Progress\nConverged to Enable Generative AI",
                 Inches(0.5), Inches(0.52), Inches(12.3), Inches(1.0),
                 size=26, bold=True, color=DARK_GRAY)

    # Three convergence pillars
    pillars = [
        ("6 Decades", "Moore's Law", "Compute horsepower to process exaflops of data"),
        ("4 Decades", "The Internet", "Trillions of tokens of training data\n(accelerated by COVID)"),
        ("2 Decades", "Mobile & Cloud", "A supercomputer in every human's palm"),
    ]

    col_w = Inches(3.8)
    col_gap = Inches(0.3)
    start_x = Inches(0.5)
    box_top = Inches(1.75)
    box_h   = Inches(4.0)

    for i, (years, title, desc) in enumerate(pillars):
        lx = start_x + i * (col_w + col_gap)

        # Background card
        add_rect(slide, lx, box_top, col_w, box_h, fill=LIGHT_GRAY)

        # Top red accent
        add_rect(slide, lx, box_top, col_w, Inches(0.07), fill=SEQ_RED)

        # Big number
        add_text_box(slide, years,
                     lx + Inches(0.15), box_top + Inches(0.18),
                     col_w - Inches(0.3), Inches(0.7),
                     size=38, bold=True, color=SEQ_RED, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

        # Pillar title
        add_text_box(slide, title,
                     lx + Inches(0.15), box_top + Inches(0.95),
                     col_w - Inches(0.3), Inches(0.55),
                     size=18, bold=True, color=DARK_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

        # Description
        add_text_box(slide, desc,
                     lx + Inches(0.2), box_top + Inches(1.6),
                     col_w - Inches(0.4), Inches(2.0),
                     size=13, color=MID_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

    # Arrow / result text
    add_rect(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(5.9), SLIDE_W - Inches(1.0), Inches(0.06), fill=RGBColor(0xDD, 0xDD, 0xDD))
    add_text_box(slide,
                 "→  ChatGPT's launch ignited a Cambrian explosion of innovation — the fastest-growing application in history",
                 Inches(0.5), Inches(6.05), SLIDE_W - Inches(1.0), Inches(0.55),
                 size=12, color=MID_GRAY, italic=True)

    add_footer_bar(slide)
    add_slide_number(slide, 2)
    return slide


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 3 – $1B Revenue
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
def slide_revenue(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout(prs))
    add_rect(slide, 0, 0, SLIDE_W, SLIDE_H, fill=WHITE)
    header_bar(slide)

    section_tag(slide, "Commercial Traction", Inches(0.5), Inches(0.18))

    add_text_box(slide,
                 "GenAI Startups Surpassed $1B Revenue\nFaster Than SaaS Ever Did",
                 Inches(0.5), Inches(0.52), Inches(12.3), Inches(1.0),
                 size=26, bold=True, color=DARK_GRAY)

    # Big stat
    add_rect(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.75), Inches(12.3), Inches(1.6), fill=RGBColor(0xF8, 0xEC, 0xED))
    add_text_box(slide, ">$1 Billion",
                 Inches(0.7), Inches(1.85), Inches(7), Inches(0.9),
                 size=44, bold=True, color=SEQ_RED)
    add_text_box(slide,
                 "in revenue from generative AI startups alone — a milestone SaaS took years, not months, to reach",
                 Inches(0.7), Inches(2.75), Inches(10.5), Inches(0.5),
                 size=13, color=DARK_GRAY)

    # Three standout companies
    cards = [
        ("ChatGPT", "OpenAI", "Fastest-growing application in history\nStrong PMF with students & developers"),
        ("Midjourney", "Midjourney", "Hundreds of millions in revenue\nTeam of just 11 people"),
        ("Character.ai", "Character Technologies", "Popularized AI companionship\n2 hours average session time"),
    ]

    col_w = Inches(3.8)
    col_gap = Inches(0.3)
    start_x = Inches(0.5)
    box_top = Inches(3.55)
    box_h   = Inches(2.8)

    for i, (app, company, desc) in enumerate(cards):
        lx = start_x + i * (col_w + col_gap)
        add_rect(slide, lx, box_top, col_w, box_h, fill=LIGHT_GRAY, line=RGBColor(0xDD, 0xDD, 0xDD))
        add_rect(slide, lx, box_top, col_w, Inches(0.06), fill=SEQ_RED)

        add_text_box(slide, app,
                     lx + Inches(0.2), box_top + Inches(0.15),
                     col_w - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.5),
                     size=20, bold=True, color=DARK_GRAY)
        add_text_box(slide, company,
                     lx + Inches(0.2), box_top + Inches(0.65),
                     col_w - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.35),
                     size=11, color=MID_GRAY, italic=True)
        add_text_box(slide, desc,
                     lx + Inches(0.2), box_top + Inches(1.1),
                     col_w - Inches(0.4), Inches(1.5),
                     size=13, color=DARK_GRAY)

    add_footer_bar(slide)
    add_slide_number(slide, 3)
    return slide


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 4 – Retention Gap (bar chart)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
def slide_retention_gap(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout(prs))
    add_rect(slide, 0, 0, SLIDE_W, SLIDE_H, fill=WHITE)
    header_bar(slide)

    section_tag(slide, "The Retention Problem", Inches(0.5), Inches(0.18))

    add_text_box(slide,
                 "AI-First Apps Show 14% Median Retention vs. 51% for Incumbents",
                 Inches(0.5), Inches(0.52), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.75),
                 size=24, bold=True, color=DARK_GRAY)

    # Two side-by-side bar charts
    incumbents = [
        ("WhatsApp", 85),
        ("Instagram", 64),
        ("YouTube", 64),
        ("TikTok", 60),
        ("Snapchat", 51),
        ("Roblox", 41),
        ("Tinder", 34),
        ("Candy Crush", 32),
        ("Duolingo", 30),
    ]
    ai_first = [
        ("Character.ai", 41),
        ("Runway", 27),
        ("Remini", 14),
        ("ChatGPT", 14),
        ("Lensa", 12),
    ]

    def draw_bars(slide, data, color, lx, top, panel_w, panel_h, median, label):
        n = len(data)
        bar_h_max = panel_h - Inches(1.0)  # leave room for labels
        bar_w = (panel_w - Inches(0.6)) / n

        # Panel background
        add_rect(slide, lx, top, panel_w, panel_h, fill=LIGHT_GRAY)

        # Panel title
        add_text_box(slide, label,
                     lx + Inches(0.1), top + Inches(0.05),
                     panel_w - Inches(0.2), Inches(0.35),
                     size=13, bold=True, color=color, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

        # Median annotation
        add_text_box(slide, f"Median: {median}%",
                     lx + Inches(0.1), top + Inches(0.42),
                     panel_w - Inches(0.2), Inches(0.28),
                     size=10, color=MID_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

        chart_top = top + Inches(0.8)
        chart_h   = panel_h - Inches(1.5)

        for j, (name, pct) in enumerate(data):
            bx = lx + Inches(0.3) + j * bar_w
            bh = chart_h * (pct / 100.0)
            by = chart_top + chart_h - bh

            add_rect(slide, bx, by, bar_w * 0.75, bh, fill=color)

            # Percentage above bar
            add_text_box(slide, f"{pct}%",
                         bx - Inches(0.05), by - Inches(0.22),
                         bar_w + Inches(0.1), Inches(0.2),
                         size=7, bold=True, color=color, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

            # App label below
            add_text_box(slide, name,
                         bx - Inches(0.05), chart_top + chart_h + Inches(0.03),
                         bar_w + Inches(0.1), Inches(0.35),
                         size=7, color=DARK_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

        # Median dashed line (simulated with thin rect)
        median_y = chart_top + chart_h - chart_h * (median / 100.0)
        add_rect(slide, lx + Inches(0.2), median_y,
                 panel_w - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.025),
                 fill=DARK_GRAY)

    panel_top = Inches(1.4)
    panel_h   = Inches(5.5)
    left_w    = Inches(7.5)
    right_w   = Inches(4.7)

    draw_bars(slide, incumbents, INCUMB_COLOR, Inches(0.3), panel_top, left_w, panel_h, 51, "Incumbent Apps")
    draw_bars(slide, ai_first,   AI_COLOR,     Inches(8.1), panel_top, right_w, panel_h, 14, "AI-First Apps")

    add_text_box(slide, "3.6× GAP",
                 Inches(0.3), panel_top + panel_h - Inches(0.5),
                 Inches(3), Inches(0.35),
                 size=11, bold=True, color=SEQ_RED)

        ("WhatsApp",     63),
        ("Roblox",       61),
        ("Tinder",       54),
        ("Duolingo",     50),
        ("Candy Crush",  48),
    ]
    median = 63

    chart_l   = Inches(2.6)
    chart_top = Inches(1.9)
    max_bar_w = Inches(9.5)
    row_h     = Inches(0.47)

    for i, (name, pct) in enumerate(data):
        row_y = chart_top + i * row_h
        bar_w = max_bar_w * (pct / 100.0)

        # App label
        add_text_box(slide, name,
                     Inches(0.35), row_y + Inches(0.06),
                     Inches(2.1), Inches(0.32),
                     size=12, color=DARK_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)

        # Bar
        add_rect(slide, chart_l, row_y + Inches(0.07), bar_w, Inches(0.3), fill=INCUMB_COLOR)

        # Pct label

                     chart_l + bar_w + Inches(0.08), row_y + Inches(0.06),
                     Inches(0.5), Inches(0.32),
                     size=12, bold=True, color=INCUMB_COLOR)

    # Median line
    median_x = chart_l + max_bar_w * (median / 100.0)
    median_row_top = chart_top - Inches(0.1)
    total_chart_h  = len(data) * row_h + Inches(0.2)
    add_rect(slide, median_x, median_row_top, Inches(0.03), total_chart_h, fill=SEQ_RED)
    add_text_box(slide, f"Median {median}%",
                 median_x - Inches(0.2), median_row_top - Inches(0.3),
                 Inches(1.2), Inches(0.28),
                 size=9, bold=True, color=SEQ_RED, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

    # Context box
    add_rect(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(6.45), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.72),
             fill=RGBColor(0xF8, 0xEC, 0xED))
    add_text_box(slide,
                 "Context: AI-first apps have a 14% median retention vs. a 63% monthly active usage benchmark for incumbents — "
                 "a formidable bar to clear for the next generation of consumer AI products.",
                 Inches(0.5), Inches(6.5), Inches(12.2), Inches(0.6),
                 size=11, color=DARK_GRAY)

    add_footer_bar(slide)
    add_slide_number(slide, 5)
    return slide

    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(1, l, t, w, h)  # MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.RECTANGLE
    shape.line.fill.background()
    if fill:
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill
    else:
        shape.fill.background()
    if line:
        shape.line.color.rgb = line
        shape.line.width = Pt(0.75)
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


def add_text_box(slide, text, l, t, w, h,
                 font_name="Calibri", size=18, bold=False,
                 color=BLACK, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                 wrap=True, italic=False):
    txb = slide.shapes.add_textbox(l, t, w, h)
    txb.word_wrap = wrap
    tf = txb.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.name = font_name
    run.font.size = Pt(size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color

        ("YouTube", 64),

    ai_first = [
        ("Character.ai", 41),
        ("Runway", 27),
        ("Remini", 14),
        ("ChatGPT", 14),
        ("Lensa", 12),
    ]

    def draw_bars(slide, data, color, lx, top, panel_w, panel_h, median, label):
        n = len(data)
        bar_h_max = panel_h - Inches(1.0)  # leave room for labels
        bar_w = (panel_w - Inches(0.6)) / n

        # Panel background
        add_rect(slide, lx, top, panel_w, panel_h, fill=LIGHT_GRAY)

        add_text_box(slide, label,
                     lx + Inches(0.1), top + Inches(0.05),

        add_text_box(slide, f"Median: {median}%",
                     lx + Inches(0.1), top + Inches(0.42),
                     panel_w - Inches(0.2), Inches(0.28),
                     size=10, color=MID_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

        chart_h   = panel_h - Inches(1.5)

        for j, (name, pct) in enumerate(data):
            bx = lx + Inches(0.3) + j * bar_w

                         bar_w + Inches(0.1), Inches(0.35),
                         size=7, color=DARK_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

        # Median dashed line (simulated with thin rect)
        median_y = chart_top + chart_h - chart_h * (median / 100.0)
        add_rect(slide, lx + Inches(0.2), median_y,
                 panel_w - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.025),
                 fill=DARK_GRAY)

    panel_top = Inches(1.4)
    panel_h   = Inches(5.5)
    left_w    = Inches(7.5)
    right_w   = Inches(4.7)

    draw_bars(slide, incumbents, INCUMB_COLOR, Inches(0.3), panel_top, left_w, panel_h, 51, "Incumbent Apps")
    draw_bars(slide, ai_first,   AI_COLOR,     Inches(8.1), panel_top, right_w, panel_h, 14, "AI-First Apps")

    return slide
